title: Assessing Demographic Bias in Named Entity Recognition
benchmark_measurement: Bias in Named Entity Recognition (NER) models against names commonly associated with Muslims.
models_tested: BILSTM CRF (with GloVe, CNET, ELMo embeddings)
findings: The study found that most Named Entity Recognition (NER) models exhibited lower accuracy for Muslim names compared to White names. For example, in the 'Winogender' dataset, the CNET model had accuracies of 0.8537 and 0.7791 for Muslim Female and Male names respectively, compared to 0.9627 and 0.9644 for White names. An exception was the character-based ELMo model, which showed the least bias across demographics and achieved the highest accuracy on Muslim Male names among all groups.
